## GC work relative to a stock generational collector

Lower is better. 100% is the stock generational collector. `gen+oracle` reads true lifetimes off a recorded trace and cannot be shipped; it is the ceiling, not a proposal.

| workload | mark-sweep | semispace | generational | gen+always | gen+sitetable | gen+learned | gen+oracle | headroom recovered |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binarytrees` | 27% | 78% | 100% | 37% | 37% | 31% | 34% | **104%** |
| `lru_cache` | 24% | 111% | 100% | 31% | 31% | 31% | 9% | **76%** |
| `particles` | 94% | 534% | 100% | 230% | 16% | 0.02% | 0.02% | **100%** |
| `graph_bfs` | 45% | 118% | 100% | 48% | 94% | 94% | 41% | **11%** |
| `doc_pipeline` | 137% | 1701% | 100% | 159% | 99% | 190% | 46% | **-168%** |

## Model quality on the held-out run

`target rate` is the fraction of objects that actually meet the learning target (live at least `K*` nurseries). Where it is 100% the profiling run chose `K* = 0`, every object is a positive, and AUC is undefined -- the model has correctly learned to pretenure everything.

| workload | AUC | precision | recall | target rate | distinct contexts scored |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binarytrees` | 0.559 | 0.922 | 0.883 | 91.4% | 113 |
| `lru_cache` | - | 1.000 | 1.000 | 100.0% | 64 |
| `particles` | 0.998 | 0.995 | 0.997 | 3.0% | 43 |
| `graph_bfs` | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.999 | 80.0% | 138 |
| `doc_pipeline` | 0.758 | 0.163 | 0.707 | 8.5% | 136 |
